record.learning: When Homebrew formula tests assert CLI JSON output, prefer a whitespace-insensitive assertion or JSON parsing; compact serializers may emit nested maps without spaces.
evidence: brew test tkersey/tap/seq initially failed on Formula/seq.rb because output contained "resolve_without_review_fold":1 while the assertion expected a space; fixing the assertion made brew audit --strict and brew test pass.
record.application: For future seq formula tests that validate JSON fields, parse the JSON or assert compact fragments instead of pretty-print spacing.

record.learning: When removing a Homebrew formula from a tap, run brew update and then check brew list plus command -v because a deleted formula can leave an installed orphaned binary on PATH until brew uninstall removes it.
evidence: st formula was absent from the workspace tap and deleted from tkersey/tap after brew update, but brew list still showed st 0.5.7 and command -v st resolved /opt/homebrew/bin/st until brew uninstall st.
record.application: For future CLI removals, verify both tap metadata and local installed command absence after updating the tap.

record.learning: When shipping a storage-migration CLI change, prefer extending the tap formula test with a damaged legacy fixture because installed-version proof must exercise repair and skip semantics, not only report the new version.
evidence: skills-zig zig build test passed 795/795; ledger-v0.5.2 release workflow 29174848180 succeeded; Formula/ledger.rb covers invalid doctor, bounded repair, source-preserving skip, and current-state verification.
record.application: Add an end-to-end damaged-store fixture to the formula before publishing future migration changes.

record.learning: When a CLI replaces capability flags, prefer updating the Homebrew formula test to assert both the retired flag is false and each replacement is true because version-and-checksum-only updates can miss a shipped contract change.
evidence: CAS 0.2.75 formula initially still asserted cas_rer_workflow_binding_v1=true; the release instead advertises that flag false plus opaque binding, history v2, and scoped instructions true.
record.application: Diff the prior formula test against the new CLI capability surface before every tap commit.

record.learning: When a Homebrew formula test verifies CLI help, prefer asserting the stable semantic capability phrase over the entire sentence because prose refinements can fail installed-version proof without signaling a behavioral regression.
evidence: brew test tkersey/tap/ledger for 0.6.1 failed only because capture help changed from the JSONL-specific sentence to the storage-neutral learning-source API sentence while the command surface remained intact.
record.application: Use targeted capability phrases in Formula/ledger.rb help assertions; reserve exact matches for protocol literals.

record.learning: When CLI help text changes to reflect a new authority or storage boundary, update Homebrew formula assertions in the same tap release and prefer a stable semantic substring; otherwise source tests can pass while brew test fails on the installed artifact.
evidence: brew test tkersey/tap/ledger failed at Formula/ledger.rb:188 on the retired physical-JSONL sentence; commit ba802ad asserted repo-local learning-source API and the rerun passed.
record.application: During tap handoff, compare formula help assertions with the released binary before declaring install closure.

record.learning: When Homebrew Actions deprecates an @master reference, prefer auditing every action from that repository across all workflows and pinning them to the same immutable CalVer commit because dormant workflows can retain the same deprecation helper.
evidence: Homebrew/actions setup-homebrew, git-user-config, and git-try-push source at 2026.07.10.1 each imports deprecateMaster; the active tap run exposed setup-homebrew while publish.yml still contained all three @master references.
record.application: Search .github/workflows for every Homebrew/actions @master reference and migrate the complete set to the producer-recommended immutable commit before CI closeout.

record.learning: When a release-relevant follow-up lands after an automatic CLI release has tagged an intermediate state, publish a new patch version and point the tap only at that final release; do not reuse or move the existing tag because tag-to-source identity must remain immutable.
evidence: Ledger 0.7.0 was tagged from c14d8c2; follow-up review-policy coverage merged as fe983d0, so VERSION advanced to 0.7.1 and the tap was rebound to the 0.7.1 archives.
record.application: Before updating a tap, compare the release tag commit with the final merged CLI source; if they differ, bump VERSION, publish a patch release, and bind the formula to the new asset digests.
